newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end lower but Ssangyong firms sparkle.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end lower but Ssangyong firms sparkle.

text.p: South Korean stocks closed sharply lower on Thursday on fears over rumours that many companies had financial troubles, brokers said.
But Ssangyong Group firms rose on news that the group was talking to General Motors Corp and other foreign firms about a $300 million capital investment in its auto unit.
The central bank's release of the first quarter gross domestic product growth figures had little immediate impact.
The composite index ended 13.33 points, or 1.81 percent, lower at 724.38.

The three listed affiliates of the Haitai Group plunged for the second straight day. The group, ranked 24th in South Korea, has been rumoured to be struggling under financial troubles. It has strongly denied the rumours.
Haitai Confectionery was down 800 won to 9,500, Haitai Electronics fell 900 won to 10,700 and Haitai Stores lost 500 won to 5,810.
"Rumours of troubles took their toll when investors were expecting a downward correction of the market following the recent rallies," said Shim Choong-bo, research manager at Daishin Securities.
Ssangyong Motor, Ssangyong Precision Industry and Ssangyong Heavy Industries went limit-up as investors hoped a deal with foreign companies would help ease financial problems at the group.
A Ssangyong Group executive told Reuters earlier on Thursday the deal would help cut Ssangyong Motor's debt-to-equity ratio to about 1,000 percent from over 10,000 percent at end-1996.
Sewon and Miwon went limit-down on an announcement that Sewon planned to absorb Miwon. Sewon fell 7,900 won to 91,600 and Miwon lost 1,700 won to 19,900.
Brokers said rumours of the merger between the two firms had circulated recently and they now had faded as a factor with the announcement.
The Bank of Korea said the nation's gross domestic product (GDP) rose by a real 5.4 percent in the first quarter of this year, against a 7.8 percent growth a year earlier.
South Korea has forecast this year's GDP growth at between five and six percent, down from an 8.1 percent growth in 1996.
June index futures closed 0.95 of a point lower at 74.15 while the underlying KOSPI-200 index shed 1.32 to 73.85.
